title: So, You Want to Live In Cohasset?

content: Photo by Craig Cole/Wavefront Media. Realtor Betsy Cornell, Corcoran Property Advisors. 1. Pick Your Price Point Limited stock and high demand mean Cohasset is a seller’s market, with median home prices routinely over $1.5 million. Single-family homes, many of which are upgraded 19th- and 20th-century properties, start at $1.2 million. For something on the waterfront, expect to pay $2.1 million on the low end. On the high end, sweeping estates with coveted addresses like Jerusalem Road go for $4 million-plus. Photo By Stuart Cahill/Boston Herald 2. Plot Your Commute Take the commuter rail from Cohasset to South Station on the Greenbush Line for an easy 45-minute journey. Without heavy traffic, commuting by car takes about the same amount of time on I-93, but during rush hour, the ride extends to an hour and a half. For a scenic route, consider driving 15 minutes to the nearby Hingham Shipyard for a 30-to-45-minute ferry ride to the city. John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe 3. Take in the Vibe Known for its quintessential New England architecture and indie businesses like French Memories bakery, Cohasset Village is the community’s hub. The Red Lion Tavern is a classic for lunch and dinner, or check out newer spots like the gastropub Hooper’s Judge . For recreation, hike Whitney and Thayer Woods or lounge at Sandy Beach (revered among locals for its private residents-only access). Courtesy of Hooper’s Judge 4. Check out the Culture Before it broke off from Hingham in the late 18th century, Cohasset was a fishing and shipbuilding community, a legacy carried on by the Cohasset Maritime Institute’s rowing programs. The South Shore Music Circus is the area’s preeminent concert venue, and the South Shore Art Center has three galleries devoted to local artists and holds more than 120 classes a year in addition to its arts festival. 5. Scope out the Schools The local district is made up of two elementary schools, one middle school, and one high school, the latter two in the same building. Other than a couple of nursery schools, there are no private options in town, but there are plenty nearby, such as Notre Dame Academy (middle and high school) and Derby Academy (elementary and middle school) in Hingham, and Inly School (elementary and middle school) in Scituate.
